newsitem.title: USA: NY utilities allowed to monitor power producers.
newsitem.headline: NY utilities allowed to monitor power producers.

text.p: The New York State Public Service Commission said it Wednesday authorized the state's seven investor-owned electric utilities to monitor independent power producers' compliance with federal "qualifying facility" -- or QF -- standards.

"If QFs are not meeting requirements," commission Chairman John O"Mara pointed out, then the obligation (of a utility) to pay the full contract rate (for the electricity produced) ... is generally excused or mitigated."
The order was in response to a petition from Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, a commission spokesman said.

The other New York electric utilities purchasing power from QFs are Long Island Lighting Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc, Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp, New York State Electric and Gas Corp and Rochester Gas and Electric Corp.

If data collected trhrough a uniform utility "QF Monitoring Program" indicates that a power producer is not meeting federal standards, the utility could petition the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to decertify the QF, NY regulators explained.

Upon decertification, the commission said, the utility could implement penalties provided for in its power purchase contract with the QF, which can include cancellation of the contract. Similar penalties could be triggered if it is determined a QF had not maintained complioance with state law.
The commission said its decision also authorizes utilities to bring actions in court against QFs that fail to satisfy reporting requirements, as federal law permits.
